cases.sentence: Николай, с несходящею улыбкой на лице, несколько изогнувшись на кресле, сидел, близко наклоняясь над блондинкой и говоря ей ___.
cases.explain: «мифологические комплименты» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Nikoláy sat leaning slightly forward in an armchair, bending closely over the blonde lady and paying her mythological compliments with a smile that never left his face. Jauntily shifting the position of his legs in their tight riding breeches, diffusing an odor of perfume, and admiring his partner, himself, and the fine outlines of his legs in their well-fitting Hessian boots, Nikoláy told the blonde lady that he wished to run away with a certain lady here in Vorónezh.

cases.sentence: ___ с неодобрительным видом подошла к ним.
cases.explain: «Добрая губернаторша» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The husband smiled gloomily, the wife gaily. The governor’s good-natured wife came up with a look of disapproval.

cases.sentence: — Анна Игнатьевна хочет тебя видеть, Nicolas, — сказала она, таким голосом выговаривая слова: Анна Игнатьевна, что Poстову сейчас стало понятно, что Анна Игнатьевна очень ___.
cases.explain: «важная дама» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Anna Ignátyevna wants to see you, Nicolas,” said she, pronouncing the name so that Nikoláy at once understood that Anna Ignátyevna was a very important person. “Come, Nicolas! You know you let me call you so?”

cases.sentence: Губернаторша подводила его к высокой и очень толстой старухе в ___, только что кончившей свою карточную партию с самыми важными лицами в городе.
cases.explain: «голубом токе» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The governor’s wife led him up to a tall and very stout old lady with a blue headdress, who had just finished her game of cards with the most important personages of the town. This was Malvíntseva, Princess Márya’s aunt on her mother’s side, a rich, childless widow who always lived in Vorónezh. When Rostóv approached her she was standing settling up for the game. She looked at him and, screwing up her eyes sternly, continued to upbraid the general who had won from her.

cases.sentence: Это была Мальвинцева, тетка княжны Марьи по матери, богатая ___, жившая всегда в Воронеже.
cases.explain: «бездетная вдова» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The governor’s wife led him up to a tall and very stout old lady with a blue headdress, who had just finished her game of cards with the most important personages of the town. This was Malvíntseva, Princess Márya’s aunt on her mother’s side, a rich, childless widow who always lived in Vorónezh. When Rostóv approached her she was standing settling up for the game. She looked at him and, screwing up her eyes sternly, continued to upbraid the general who had won from her.

cases.sentence: Николай вдруг почувствовал желание и необходимость рассказать все свои ___ (такие, которые не рассказал бы и матери, сестре, другу) этой почти чужой женщине.
cases.explain: «задушевные мысли» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Nikoláy suddenly felt a desire and need to tell his most intimate thoughts (which he would not have told to his mother, his sister, or his friend) to this woman who was almost a stranger. When he afterwards recalled that impulse to unsolicited and inexplicable frankness which had very important results for him, it seemed to him—as it seems to everyone in such cases—that it was merely some silly whim that seized him: yet that burst of frankness, together with other trifling events, had immense consequences for him and for all his family.
